Hi team,

Attaching this week's pipeline snapshot and the reserve-slot demand model we ran overnight (see attachments). StratusCloud confirmed their Q3 pilot expansion is likely to move from a 2-node POC to a 12-node reserved cadence if the perf numbers hold. Tom (cc'd) will confirm timelines later today.

As a reminder, the goal for this thread: produce a tight recommendation for how many reserved slots to hold as we approach the June close window, balancing:
- Probabilistic deal conversion (we've got a 40% lift for Stratus if benchmarks are within 20% of our hosted latency)
- Finance runway — cap on committed slots before Exec sign-off
- Infra lead times for additional GPUs (rack/spare capacity and procurement can take ~6–8 weeks for reserved pools)

Quick asks:
1) Ben — can you confirm expected close probability movement after today's benchmarks and if legal procurement needs additional lead time?
2) Laura — what flexible threshold do you need to green-light an extra 8 reserved slots for one quarter?
3) Marissa/Karthik — realistic timeline to provision and the minimum burst buffer we should hold while waiting for reserve commit?

I propose we meet Thursday 10:00 PT for a 30-minute decision call; if we can align by EOD Friday with an action list, ops can start slot reservations next Monday.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes

Camila — thanks for the clear ask and the model. Short update from sales: Stratus ran perf tests this morning; initial feed looks favorable but they want the second benchmark (longer context, 1M token run) before giving product recommendation to their procurement team. If that passes, legal + procurement typically turn around a standard MSA + SOW in ~10 business days for this account.

Conservative schedule: assume a verbal go from Stratus next Thu (5/23), signed PO by 6/6. Upside: if legal accepts standard terms faster, PO could arrive before end of May.

I'll bring a probability ladder to Thursday's call (belt-and-suspenders, mid, optimistic) — right now my working forecast is:
- Base: 40% convert -> 8 reserved slots for 3 months
- Upside: 65% convert -> 16 slots + burst credits
- Downside: 15% convert -> no reserve, continue burst usage

Thanks — quick finance constraints: we can authorize incremental reserved spend up to $75k/mo off-deck for targeted pilots (requires Director sign-off). Anything above that threshold needs VP approval and a multi-quarter commitment. For Stratus, an 8-slot quarter at our quoted rates would be ~$60–68k/mo depending on quantization/slot sizing. 16 slots pushes us into VP territory unless we compress term to one quarter with a firm PO.

Ask for the decision call: if sales wants the < $75k pathway, we need a documented risk register (what happens if the pilot doesn't convert) and a rollback plan (auto-stop and burst fallback). If the execs sign off for >$75k, procurement will want a heads-up 7–10 business days before PO issuance so they can clear commercial terms.

Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Reserve slot tradecraft — weekly sync: pipeline signals -> fleet sizing

Operational constraints from infra: current lead time for reserved GPU slots is still 6 weeks if we need new capacity on a dedicated cluster (procurement + rack + provisioning). We have three potential levers to shorten the customer-visible gap:
1) Burst buffer: keep 12 burst-capable slots across regions (costlier per-token but immediate)
2) Shiftable pool: reallocate 4–6 slots from low-usage internal demo pools for 4–6 weeks (minimal customer impact)
3) Fast-path procurement: requires finance pre-approval (Laura) to spin up a short-term lease; can cut to ~3 weeks but costs a ~25% premium.

Recommendation for the call: aim to hold a 10-slot conservative reserve (6 dedicated + 4 burst) under the <$75k authorization path — this buys us runway to wait for signed PO while keeping performance SLOs intact. If sales moves to the 16-slot ask, we escalate to VP for the pre-approval and plan the fast-path procurement.

Marissa
